name: Run Meta Progression
description: What death buys you. Between runs, a persistent unlock pool — new cards, characters, starting items, difficulty tiers — is purchased with meta currency earned from run performance, so even a floor-two faceplant moves the account forward. It owns the pool, the prices, and the balance, written through persistence.save_system immediately on every purchase and grant, because meta progress lost to a crash teaches players to fear the save system instead of the dungeon. It pairs deliberately with progression.permadeath_flag: permadeath makes the run's end matter, this makes the ending matter differently, and neither is a complete roguelike alone. It does not own in-run power — run-scoped modifiers such as relics die with the run and never enter this pool — and it does not judge run performance; the credit grant arrives, this component banks it.

inputs.name: unlockPool
inputs.description: Purchasable unlocks as {id, price, prerequisiteIds}. Required because an empty pool is a progression screen with nothing to say.

inputs.name: startingUnlockIds
inputs.description: Unlocks a fresh profile already holds. The baseline kit every player starts with; keep it small enough that the pool still has somewhere to go.

inputs.name: deathCreditBase
inputs.description: Currency granted at run end before performance bonuses. Non-zero by design: a run that pays nothing on death trains players to quit at the first bad floor.

outputs.name: unlockedIds
outputs.description: Everything the profile has permanently unlocked, in purchase order.
